He explains the code he used to create a "Twitter scraper" to scrap all of Trump's tweets. Twitter created an API for developers to be able to use Twitter data in their own applications. An API is a way for one system to get data to another system.

Websites have a "back end" database or multiple databases where every thing is stored and a "front end" which controls how that information is loaded in the web browser for the customer. On a Voat, pages, comments scroll down the page because that is how the front templates work, but you could design a different template where comments scrolled right to left without changing the back end whatsoever.

Websites also need a data exchange layer, the thing that gets the data from the back end to the front end. One really popular technology for this is called JSON.

JSON is

a data interchange format that has vastly improved server-to-browser communications— ...and a syntax designed to store and move data that’s sent between server and browser.

Developers like this because it's a little bit faster and easier to use than previous technologies which means less work for the database and quicker page loads.
